messages:
maya: FYI starting canary bring-up of osmium14b (14B) quantized to int4 on canary pool. Running summarization eval; seeing quality drop and occasional OOMs when max_new_tokens >= 512. Will paste quick notes and logs.
ian: Link to the bench artifacts?
maya: Quick summary in the artifacts bucket: s3://redwood-bench/osmium14b/int4/sanity-2026-03-23. Numbers: p95 latency up ~10%, cost down ~30%, ROUGE-L -4, ROUGE-1 -6 vs fp16 baseline. Repro: `scripts/eval.sh --model osmium14b --quant int4 --suite summarization --max_new_tokens 512`
su: Can you paste the worker stderr where OOM happened?
maya: paste: ```ERROR: CUDA out of memory while allocating 1.2 GiB
RuntimeError: slot allocator failed to reserve 256MB
...at runtime/slot_allocator.cc:234
Allocation timeline: prefetch->kv_load->generation```
ben: That stack + "slot allocator" smells like fragmentation with prefetch + big max_new_tokens. Did you enable prefetch? what's prefetch_window and batch config?
maya: prefetch_window=128, microbatch_size=1, batch_size=8, kv_evict_threshold=0.5 (defaults).
ian: Two quick experiments: 1) reduce prefetch_window to 32, 2) lower default max_new_tokens to 256 for canary. Also try `prefetch_padding=32` to avoid tight allocations.
su: Quant layout can exacerbate slab fragmentation; even though total free memory is OK, contiguous block for large alloc fails. Can you repro with `--max_new_tokens 256 --prefetch_window 32`?
maya: Kicking that now. deploy-bot: starting canary deploy: osmium14b-int4 -> pool-canary-3
deploy-bot: :rocket: canary deploy started for osmium14b-int4 on pool-canary-3
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: canary pod 3 ready (image v2026-03-23-int4)
maya: Quick update: with max_new_tokens=256 + prefetch_window=32, ran 200 sample requests, p95 latency down to ~210ms, zero OOM hits so far. Quality delta narrowed: ROUGE-L now -3 vs baseline.
ben: Sounds like prefetch window + big max_new_tokens is the root cause for the OOMs. For longer summaries we should add adaptive_prefetch (grow with context but cap) and a soft-default for max_new_tokens on new quantized models. I'll prototype a "kv-compact-on-alloc" step to reduce fragmentation before large allocations.
ial: (typo) ignore
alina: Filed ML-1421: "osmium14b int4 onboarding: conservative max_new_tokens default + prefetch heuristics".
ian: Plan of action: 1) rollback runtime defaults for canary to max_new_tokens=256 for new int4 models, 2) expose per-model prefetch_window override in model config, 3) add kv-compact/soft-evict pause on large allocation attempts. Ben, can you own runtime patch?
ben: I'll take it. Will prototype kv-compact in a feature branch and run microbench against canary.
su: I'll run the full eval sweep (summarization+longform) with the new config to see if quality regressions persist or if it's a side-effect of truncation. Also will check attention patterns for compression artifacts.
maya: Next steps: I'll run the larger sweep and post final logs here. For immediate canary stability I'll keep max_new_tokens=256 and prefetch_window=32.
maya: Thanks everyone — will update when full sweep completes. :thumbsup:
